claim: Human-associated microbial communities vary across individuals due to factors including genetic relatedness, diet, and age.
source_text: Human-associated microbial communities vary across individuals: possible contributing factors include (genetic) relatedness, diet, and age.
evidence_reasoning: This statement draws from established scientific understanding and is supported by references to prior work in the field.

claim: Surroundings and individuals with whom we interact likely shape our microbial communities.
source_text: However, our surroundings, including individuals with whom we interact, also likely shape our microbial communities.
evidence_reasoning: This is presented as a hypothesis or likely scenario based on logical reasoning, not yet definitively proven.

claim: The study surveyed fecal, oral, and skin microbiota from 60 families with various compositions.
source_text: To quantify this microbial exchange, we surveyed fecal, oral, and skin microbiota from 60 families (spousal units with children, dogs, both, or neither).
evidence_reasoning: This describes the actual experimental design and data collection performed in the study.

claim: Household members, particularly couples, shared more of their microbiota than individuals from different households.
source_text: Household members, particularly couples, shared more of their microbiota than individuals from different households
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary finding directly supported by experimental measurements and analysis.

claim: Co-habitation has stronger effects on skin microbiota than oral or fecal microbiota.
source_text: with stronger effects of co-habitation on skin than oral or fecal microbiota
evidence_reasoning: This is a comparative finding based on direct measurements across different body sites.

claim: Dog ownership significantly increased the shared skin microbiota in cohabiting adults.
source_text: Dog ownership significantly increased the shared skin microbiota in cohabiting adults
evidence_reasoning: This is a specific finding supported by statistical analysis of the collected data.

claim: Dog-owning adults shared more skin microbiota with their own dogs than with other dogs.
source_text: dog-owning adults shared more 'skin' microbiota with their own dogs than with other dogs
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct finding from comparative analysis of microbiota sharing patterns.

claim: Direct and frequent contact with cohabitants may significantly shape the composition of microbial communities.
source_text: these results suggest that direct and frequent contact with our cohabitants may significantly shape the composition of our microbial communities
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the experimental results, presented as a suggested conclusion.

claim: Genetically related individuals tend to share more of their gut (fecal) microbes than unrelated individuals, regardless of whether they cohabitate at the time of sampling.
source_text: Genetically related individuals, regardless of whether they cohabitate or not at the time of sampling, tend to share more of their gut (fecal) microbes than unrelated individuals
evidence_reasoning: This statement is supported by multiple citations to previous studies (Caugant et al., 1984; Zoetendal et al., 2001; Stewart et al., 2005; Rajilić-Stojanović et al., 2007; Turnbaugh et al., 2008).

claim: Monozygotic twins are not significantly more similar than dizygotic twins in their gut microbiota.
source_text: However, monozygotic twins are not significantly more similar than dizygotic twins
evidence_reasoning: This finding is attributed to a previous study (Turnbaugh et al., 2008).

claim: The effect of genetic relatedness on gut microbiota similarity may be influenced by more than genetic similarity.
source_text: indicating that this effect may be influenced by more than genetic similarity
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the observation about monozygotic vs dizygotic twins.

claim: The fecal microbiota of teens was more similar to that of their parents than unrelated adults.
source_text: we observed that the composition of the fecal microbiota of teens was more similar to that of their parents than unrelated adults
evidence_reasoning: This refers to findings from a previous study by the authors (Yatsunenko et al., 2012).

claim: Mothers and fathers shared more similar bacterial communities in their guts compared to unrelated individuals living in other households.
source_text: Moreover, mothers and fathers shared more similar bacterial communities in their guts compared to unrelated individuals living in other households
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from a previous study (Yatsunenko et al., 2012).

claim: A shared environment or lifestyle affects the similarity of the fecal microbiota.
source_text: indicating that a shared environment or lifestyle (e.g., contact with same microbial sources or diet) affects the similarity of the fecal microbiota
evidence_reasoning: This is an interpretation of findings from a previous study.

claim: Family members may share intestinal bacteria with their household pets.
source_text: Family members may also share intestinal bacteria with their household pets
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by a citation to Caugant et al., 1984.

claim: We leave microbes from our bodies on the surfaces we touch.
source_text: Because we leave microbes from our bodies on the surfaces we touch
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations (Fierer et al., 2010; Flores et al., 2011) and is established knowledge.

claim: At least a moderate level of microbial exchange is facilitated by direct contact.
source_text: at least a moderate level of microbial exchange is facilitated by direct contact
evidence_reasoning: This is a reasonable inference based on established understanding of microbial transfer.

claim: Body site-associated microbial communities may be shaped in part by our surroundings and those we contact on a daily basis.
source_text: it is conceivable that our body site-associated microbial communities are shaped in part by our surroundings and those we contact on a daily basis
evidence_reasoning: This is presented as a conceivable hypothesis based on logical reasoning.

claim: The study examined 159 individuals comprising 17 families with cohabiting children aged 6 months to 18 years, 17 families with one or more dogs but no children, 8 families with both children and dogs, and 18 families with neither children nor dogs.
source_text: We sampled 159 individuals comprising 17 families with cohabiting children aged 6 months to 18 years, 17 families with one or more dogs but no children, 8 families with both children and dogs, and 18 families with neither children nor dogs.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the actual study design and sample composition.

claim: Each family consisted of at least two cohabiting adults between the ages of 26 and 87 years.
source_text: Each family consisted of at least two cohabiting adults (which we define as 'partners' or 'couples') between the ages of 26 and 87 years
evidence_reasoning: This describes the study population characteristics.

claim: All children included in this study were biologically related to and cohabited with the focal couple.
source_text: all children included in this study were biologically related to and cohabited with the focal couple
evidence_reasoning: This describes a criterion for inclusion in the study.

claim: For humans, fecal, oral (dorsal tongue), forehead, and right and left palm communities were sampled (n = 5 samples per individual all taken at a single time point).
source_text: For humans, fecal, oral (dorsal tongue), forehead, and right and left palm communities were sampled (n = 5 samples per individual all taken at a single time point).
evidence_reasoning: This describes the sampling methodology.

claim: Dogs were sampled similarly except that all four paws were swabbed (n = 7 samples per dog taken at the same time that humans were sampled).
source_text: Dogs were sampled similarly (n = 36), except that all four paws were swabbed (n = 7 samples per dog taken at the same time that humans were sampled).
evidence_reasoning: This describes the sampling methodology for dogs.

claim: A total of 969 samples were used for the analyses reported, with 74,855,127 total reads and an average read length of 105 ± 19 nt.
source_text: n = 969 samples used for the analyses reported, 74,855,127 total reads; average read length, 105 ± 19 nt
evidence_reasoning: This provides specific quantitative details about the sequencing data.

claim: Family membership explained a large proportion of the variability in bacterial diversity across all body sites.
source_text: Our results revealed that family unit had a strong effect on human microbial community composition across all body sites: at each site, family membership explained a large proportion of the variability in bacterial diversity
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary finding from statistical analysis of the data.

claim: For tongue and feces, effects were observed at the level of family and partner, although generally of smaller magnitude than for skin sites (R < 0.30).
source_text: For tongue and feces, we observed effects at the level of family and partner, although generally of smaller magnitude than for skin sites (R < 0.30).
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative finding from the analysis with specific R values provided.

claim: The comparison between partners is the strongest for all body sites and likely drives similarities by family at these sites.
source_text: The comparison between partners, which is nested within the comparison between family members, is the strongest for all body sites and likely drives similarities by family at these sites.
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from the data with an interpretive inference about the mechanism.

claim: A weaker effect, or no effect, was observed for parent–offspring pairs (R < 0.15).
source_text: In contrast, a weaker effect, or no effect, was observed for parent–offspring pairs (Figure 1C,D, R < 0.15).
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative finding with specific R values.

claim: Parents may share significantly more similar tongue and gut communities with their own children than with other children at older ages (3–18 years), but the same is not the case for parents and their infants.
source_text: Although parents may share significantly more similar tongue and gut communities with their own children than with other children at older ages (3–18 years), the same is not the case for parents and their infants.
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from age-stratified analysis of the data.

claim: Effects of cohabitation are insufficiently strong to overcome differences due to age, particularly between infants and adults.
source_text: However, our results also suggest that effects of cohabitation are insufficiently strong to overcome differences due to age (which are discussed in more detail in the section 'Effect of age on the human microbiota'), particularly between infants and adults, whose microbiota differ substantially
evidence_reasoning: This is an interpretation of the findings regarding age effects.

claim: The microbiota of infants and adults differ substantially.
source_text: particularly between infants and adults, whose microbiota differ substantially
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations (Palmer et al., 2007; Koenig et al., 2011) and is established knowledge.

claim: A shared environment may homogenize skin communities through contact with common surfaces (including each other).
source_text: We concluded that a shared environment may homogenize skin communities through contact with common surfaces (including each other).
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion drawn from the observed patterns in the data.

claim: It may be easier to exchange skin microbes via exposure to home surfaces or indoor air than it is to exchange gut or mouth bacteria.
source_text: Likewise, it may be easier to exchange skin microbes via exposure to home surfaces or indoor air (both of which are typically dominated by skin-associated microbes ; Fierer et al., 2010), than it is to exchange gut or mouth bacteria
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference based on the findings and supported by a citation about surface microbiota.

claim: Home surfaces and indoor air are typically dominated by skin-associated microbes.
source_text: both of which are typically dominated by skin-associated microbes ; Fierer et al., 2010
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by a citation to Fierer et al., 2010.

claim: Skin surfaces may be less 'selective' environments compared to the gut or mouth environments.
source_text: potentially because skin surfaces may be less 'selective' environments compared to the gut or mouth environments
evidence_reasoning: This is presented as a potential explanation, indicating speculative reasoning.

claim: Observed microbiota developmental dynamics depend on the body site under consideration.
source_text: Our results suggest that observed microbiota developmental dynamics depend on the body site under consideration
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion drawn from analysis of different body sites.

claim: Taxa driving differences on the palm are lineages commonly reported in surveys of the human skin microbiota such as Propionibacteria.
source_text: The taxa driving these differences on the palm are lineages commonly reported in surveys of the human skin microbiota such as Propionibacteria
evidence_reasoning: This identifies specific taxa from the data and references established knowledge about skin microbiota.

claim: Two taxa, Prevotella and Veillonella, are primarily associated with the human oral community.
source_text: Two of these taxa, Prevotella and Veillonella, are primarily associated with the human oral community
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by a citation (Nasidze et al., 2009).

claim: For cohabiting couples, oral-skin transfer may be moderately frequent.
source_text: suggesting that at least for cohabiting couples, oral-skin transfer may be moderately frequent
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference based on the presence of oral-associated taxa on skin.

claim: On average, approximately 11% of the palm community is likely from oral sources, as opposed to <2% from fecal sources.
source_text: Using SourceTracker (Knights et al., 2011), we estimated that on average, ∼11% of the palm community is likely from oral sources, as opposed to <2% from fecal sources.
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative finding from computational analysis using SourceTracker.

claim: Oral bacteria can persist on skin for at least 8 hr.
source_text: Given that oral bacteria can persist on skin for at least 8 hr
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by a citation (Costello et al., 2009).

claim: Close physical contact (such as that between cohabiting couples) can affect the taxonomic composition of the skin.
source_text: However, these results do suggest that close physical contact (such as that between cohabiting couples) can affect the taxonomic composition of the skin
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion drawn from the observed patterns of shared taxa.

claim: The similarity in the microbiota of cohabiting individuals extends beyond human-to-human relationships to pet-to-pet and even human-to-pet relationships.
source_text: Interestingly, the similarity in the microbiota of cohabiting individuals extends beyond human-to-human relationships to pet-to-pet and even human-to-pet relationships.
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from analysis of both human and pet samples.

claim: The patterns of similarity between cohabiting dogs mimic that of cohabiting people, with skin (fur) sites showing the greatest degree of similarity.
source_text: The patterns of similarity between cohabiting dogs mimic that of cohabiting people, with skin (fur) sites showing the greatest degree of similarity
evidence_reasoning: This is a comparative finding from analysis of dog samples.

claim: Dogs appear to have the largest effect on the skin communities of their cohabiting adult owners.
source_text: Because dogs appear to have the largest effect on the skin communities of their cohabiting adult owners
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from comparative analysis of dog-owning vs non-dog-owning households.

claim: Adults who have dogs share more bacterial phylotypes with each other than they do with adults who do not have dogs.
source_text: Adults who have dogs share more bacterial phylotypes with each other than they do with adults who do not have dogs
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative finding from phylotype sharing analysis.

claim: Effects of gender or dogs were not detected in the gut or oral communities.
source_text: In contrast to the skin communities, effects of gender or dogs were not detected in the gut or oral communities
evidence_reasoning: This is a negative finding from statistical analysis.

claim: Owning other types of indoor pets (i.e., cats) did not have a significant effect on the diversity, overall similarity, or amount of taxa shared between the skin communities of adult partners.
source_text: Curiously, owning other types of indoor pets (i.e., cats [which were not sampled for this study]) did not have a significant effect on the diversity (Table 7), overall similarity (Table 5), or amount of taxa shared between the skin communities of adult partners (p=0.92, Wilcoxon test).
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from statistical analysis with specific p-value reported.

claim: Having a child did not have a comparable effect to age or dog ownership on community similarity or diversity.
source_text: having a child in our study cohort also did not have a comparable effect to age or dog ownership on community similarity or diversity
evidence_reasoning: This is a comparative finding from statistical analysis.

claim: Family size only explained a small proportion of the variability in diversity across all body sites (oral: 0%, palms: <1%, fecal: 3%, forehead: 8%) compared to age (oral: 36%, palms: 17%, fecal: 46%, forehead: 15%).
source_text: For example, family size only explained a small proportion of the variability in diversity across all body sites (oral: 0%, palms: <1%, fecal: 3%, forehead: 8%) compared to age (oral: 36%, palms: 17%, fecal: 46%, forehead: 15%).
evidence_reasoning: This provides specific quantitative results from variance analysis.

claim: One of the main taxa driving the pattern of similarity between dog owners is a family of Betaproteobacteria (Methylophilaceae), a group that was highly abundant (4.6%) in the mouths of the dogs in this study.
source_text: One of the main taxa driving the pattern of similarity between dog owners is a family of Betaproteobacteria (Methylophilaceae), a group that was also highly abundant (4.6%) in the mouths of the dogs in this study
evidence_reasoning: This identifies specific taxa from the data with quantitative abundance information.

claim: The presence of Methylophilaceae is consistent with a common occurrence of oral–skin transfer between dogs and their owners.
source_text: consistent with a common occurrence of oral–skin transfer between dogs and their owners
evidence_reasoning: This is an interpretation of the taxonomic findings.

claim: Recent studies in gnotobiotic and other animal models show pervasive effects of the microbiota on metabolism, immunity, and other aspects of biology.
source_text: Given that recent studies in gnotobiotic and other animal models show pervasive effects of the microbiota on metabolism, immunity, and other aspects of our biology
evidence_reasoning: This references established findings from the broader scientific literature.

claim: Who we cohabit with, including companion animals, may alter our physiological properties by influencing the consortia of microbial symbionts that we harbor.
source_text: it is intriguing to consider that who we cohabit with, including companion animals, may alter our physiological properties by influencing the consortia of microbial symbionts that we harbor in and on our various body habitats
evidence_reasoning: This is presented as a speculative consideration based on the findings.

claim: The hygiene hypothesis posits that a broad range of microbial exposures helps educate our developing immune systems to tolerate a variety of environmental antigens, thereby reducing risk for atopic disorders such as asthma and food allergies.
source_text: One example relates to the hygiene hypothesis, which posits that a broad range of microbial exposures helps educate our developing immune systems to tolerate a variety of environmental antigens, thereby reducing risk for atopic disorders such as asthma and food allergies.
evidence_reasoning: This describes an established hypothesis in the field.

claim: Recent studies link early exposure to pets to decreased prevalence of allergies, respiratory conditions, and other immune disorders in later stages of development.
source_text: Recent studies link early exposure to pets to decreased prevalence of allergies, respiratory conditions, and other immune disorders in later stages of development
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by a citation (Havstad et al., 2011).

claim: Skin microbes are now receiving more focus as important players in immune regulation.
source_text: skin microbes in particular are now receiving more focus as important players in immune regulation
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by a citation (Naik et al., 2012) and reflects current research trends.

claim: Skin has potential as a collector and integrator of shared environmental bacteria.
source_text: Given the potential of skin as a collector and integrator of shared environmental bacteria as demonstrated in this study
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion drawn from the study's findings.

claim: The V2 region of bacterial 16S rRNA genes was amplified using the primers F27 and R338 barcoded with a unique 12-base error-correcting Golay code for multiplexing.
source_text: For each sample, the V2 region of bacterial 16S rRNA genes was amplified in triplicate reactions using the primers F27 (5′-AGAGTTTGATCCTGGCTCAG-3′) and R338 (5′-TGCTGCCTCCCGTAGGAG T-3′) barcoded with a unique12-base error-correcting Golay code for multiplexing.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the specific molecular methods used in the study.

claim: Multiplex DNA sequencing was performed with an Illumina GAIIx instrument.
source_text: Multiplex DNA sequencing was performed with a Illumina GAIIx instrument located in the Center for Genome Sciences and Systems Biology at Washington University School of Medicine.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the sequencing technology and location used.

claim: Sequences were clustered against the Greengenes database at 97% identity.
source_text: Briefly, sequences were clustered against the Greengenes database (reference collection, 2011 release) (http://greengenes.lbl.gov/) at 97% identity
evidence_reasoning: This describes the bioinformatic analysis method used.

claim: For the 1076 samples, the number of sequences per sample ranged from 1 to 300,473, with a mean of 54,475 sequences per sample (total: 58,615,414).
source_text: For the 1076 samples, the number of sequences per sample ranged from 1 to 300,473, with a mean of 54,475 sequences per sample (total: 58,615,414).
evidence_reasoning: This provides specific quantitative details about the sequencing output.

claim: Large variability in the number of sequences per sample is typical for studies employing high-throughput sequencing methods.
source_text: Such large variability in the number of sequences per sample is typical for studies employing high-throughput sequencing methods
evidence_reasoning: This reflects established understanding of sequencing technology characteristics.

claim: Samples with <5000 sequences per sample were removed from analysis.
source_text: To standardize sequence counts across samples, samples with <5000 sequences per sample were removed.
evidence_reasoning: This describes a quality control step in the data processing.

claim: Alpha diversity estimates such as PD and OTU counts may be overestimated due to sequencing error in Illumina data.
source_text: Because there are no generally accepted methods for 'denoising' Illumina sequence data, alpha diversity estimates such as PD and OTU counts may be overestimated due to sequencing error.
evidence_reasoning: This acknowledges a known limitation of the sequencing technology.

claim: Overestimation of alpha diversity should not affect relative differences in diversity.
source_text: However, overestimation should not affect relative differences in diversity.
evidence_reasoning: This is a logical inference about the impact of systematic error on comparative analyses.
